idiom_name: top-level functions in a facade file; class delegation with `by` when an interface must be forwarded
implementation_notes: Kotlin facades are usually a file of top-level functions (compiled into a FileKt class) over internal collaborators, or an object when a single entry point is wanted; a wrapper class is unnecessary while the facade is stateless. When the facade must implement an interface, use class delegation - `class SdkFacade(a: FeatureA, b: FeatureB) : FeatureA by a, FeatureB by b` - so forwarding is generated with zero boilerplate and only the members needing custom coordination are overridden. Switch to a class when collaborators must be injected or the facade carries configuration.
pitfalls: Top-level functions cannot be injected or substituted, so callers cannot be isolated from the subsystem in tests; use a class with a defaultable constructor parameter when that matters.
Delegation with `by` silently forwards members; a member shared by two delegated interfaces must be overridden explicitly or the compiler rejects the class as ambiguous.
A facade of defaults-heavy overloads grows into an unreadable signature wall; expose one method per task instead of every subsystem option.
